en: Itivuttaka 53: Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, when the venerable Ānanda had understood that the Blessed One had risen from his seat and entered his dwelling, he addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is intent on the destruction of suffering, yet does not understand as it really is: 'This is suffering'; does not understand as it really is: 'This is the origin of suffering'; does not understand as it really is:

'This is the cessation of suffering'; and does not understand as it really is: 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering. This, friends, is the first kind of person found existing in the world. Then again, friends, there is the person who is intent on the destruction of suffering, and understands as it really is: 'This is suffering'; understands as it really is: 'This is the origin of suffering'; understands as it really is: 'This is the cessation of suffering'; and understands as it really is: 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' yet does not practice the way leading to the cessation of suffering. This, friends, is the second kind of person found existing in the world. Then again, friends, there is the person who is intent on the destruction of suffering, and understands as it really is: 'This is suffering'; understands as it really is: 'This is the origin of suffering'; understands as it really is: 'This is the cessation of suffering'; and understands as it really is: 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' and practices the way leading to the cessation of suffering. This, friends, is the third kind of person found existing in the world. These, friends, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Ānanda: "Friend Ānanda, it is well said; friend Ānanda, it is well said. For one who has not understood as it really is: 'This is suffering'... 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' it is impossible to realize the fruit of stream-entry. But for one who has understood as it really is: 'This is suffering'... 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' it is possible to realize the fruit of stream-entry. For one who has not understood as it really is: 'This is suffering'... 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' it is impossible to realize the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... the fruit of arahantship. But for one who has understood as it really is: 'This is suffering'... 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' it is possible to realize the fruit of arahantship. The Second Discourse on Feelings.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings."
Which three?
Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Pleasant feeling, monks, should be viewed as suffering.
Painful feeling should be seen as a dart;
neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling should be seen as impermanent.
But when, monks, a monk has seen pleasant feeling as suffering, painful feeling as a dart, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as impermanent;
“Monks, this is called a monk who is noble, one who sees rightly; he has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and through the complete penetration of conceit, he has made an end of suffering.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“He who saw pleasure as suffering,
and saw suffering as a dart, and saw the peaceful state that is neither-suffering-nor-pleasure— ”
He saw it as impermanent.
That bhikkhu is indeed one of right vision,
since he is liberated from that.
“The sage who has reached the culmination of direct knowledge and is at peace is indeed one who has transcended all bonds.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth.
